newsitem.title: UK: UK Fulmar on schedule to join Ekofisk by end-Jan.
newsitem.headline: UK Fulmar on schedule to join Ekofisk by end-Jan.

text.p: Shell's UK North Sea Fulmar blend oilfield system remains on schedule to start pumping crude via a new link to the Norpipe system by the end of January, a Shell spokesman said.

Fulmar Blend, which collects some 125,000 barrels per day (bpd) of crude, from the Fulmar, Gannet, Clyde, Auk and Leven fields, will be delivered via Phillips Petroleum Norpipe to the company's Teesside terminal in northeast England.
Fulmar Blend will be mixed with Ekofisk output, increasing the Ekofisk stream to some 650,000 bpd, the terminal operator estimates.
Fulmar currently is delivered to northwest European refineries by shuttle tankers which load direct from a floating production and storage unit.
Norpipe delivers Norway's Ekofisk area crude and oil from six other Norwegian satellite fields to Teesside.
The stream will be increased further when Phillips' 65,000 bpd British J-block fields come onstream in May.
